hyperendorphinemia is an important feature in obesity and that it is not influenced by slimming.
the high plasmatic levels and the persistence of hyperendorphinemia after weight reduction, could be the cause of the hyperphagy and of the persistence of obesity.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hyperendorphinemic condition in obese subjects, which is not related to the ACTH level, is not a transient phenomenon, but is a stable state, even after the reduction of fat mass.
in obese patients, hyperendorphinemia is a marker of obesity and not of weight-loss.

the hyperendorphinemic condition is a marker of obesity, and that the reduction of body-weight, obtained with diet or with the association of an anorectic drug, is able to reduce hyperphagia and hyperendorphinemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hyperendorphinemic condition persists after the weight-loss, even if the body weight has been reduced.
the serotoninergic anorexigenic treatment does not modify the behaviour of plasmatic B-Ep levels.
the serotoninergic anorexigenic drug does not influence the hyperendorphinic state, but, in the obese patients, it is able to induce a significant reduction of body weight.
